title: Wurtz Alkane Synthesis
aim: Perform a coupling reaction using methyl chloride and sodium metal in dry ether to synthesize symmetric higher alkanes (ethane).
theory: The Wurtz reaction is an organic coupling reaction where two alkyl halides are reacted with sodium metal in dry ether solvent to form a symmetric higher alkane. Equation: 2 R-X + 2 Na -> R-R + 2 NaX.
procedure: Assemble reactants in dry flask under nitrogen blanket.
Add 2 moles of methyl chloride in dry ether.
Reflux the mixture gently to facilitate coupling.
observations: Intense exothermic reaction upon sodium addition.
Formation of white sodium chloride precipitate.
result: Ethane (C2H6) is successfully synthesized through Wurtz coupling.

viva_questions.question: Why is dry ether used as a solvent in the Wurtz reaction?
viva_questions.answer: Sodium is highly reactive with moisture/water. Dry ether provides an inert, anhydrous medium.

viva_questions.question: Can methane be prepared by the Wurtz reaction?
viva_questions.answer: No, because Wurtz coupling requires joining of two carbon fragments, producing symmetrical alkanes with at least two carbons.
